quote: surprise began to diminish as my knowledge increased; and I ceased to feel those apprehensions and alarms
decision: Sustained exposure to a new environment calibrates alarm down as knowledge accrues.
why: familiarity data lowers threat response, the way warm state lowers cold-start fear

quote: go ashore and be flogged round the town, without judge or jury
decision: Documented free status gave no protection where the local forum refused to recognize it.
why: receipts alone do not shield a seat when the adjudicating surface denies them standing

quote: for asking a gentleman that he worked for for the money he had earned, was put into gaol
decision: Demanding owed wages could land the creditor in jail when no registry backed the debt.
why: an earnings claim without a records surface inverts creditor into criminal

quote: But you confirm her in the wrong way.
decision: Amusing oneself with a learner's errors and inviting their repetition cements the mistakes.
why: rewarding wrong outputs for entertainment trains the error in; graders must never reinforce it

quote: There's a God for you, but is there any for us?
decision: Trust doctrines read differently from exposed versus protected positions.
why: one seat's reliable guarantor is another seat's absent one; trust is position-dependent

quote: It is better that a dozen slaves should suffer under the lash, than that the overseer should be convicted
decision: A regime where accusation equals conviction and exposure of fault is punished above the fault itself.
why: the bytes name the exact failure mode verify-before-trust and proof-before-verdict exist to invert

quote: it could do no harm, if it did no good
decision: Unfalsifiable remedies persist because their cost is zero and no test can fail them.
why: charms pass where no falsifier exists; the estate wants checks that can fail

quote: His fallacies were exposed to full view by Regiomontanus.
decision: Each circle-squaring claim was met by an opposing mathematician who exposed its fallacies.
why: pairing every claimant with an adversarial checker mirrors the grading-fan pattern

quote: That these proofs would lack rigor was almost to be expected, as long as no distinction was made
decision: Proofs lacked rigor until the right distinction between proof classes was drawn.
why: rigor follows typed distinctions; gates without categories cannot judge soundly

quote: a result previously deduced by E. Picard
decision: Every result is filed with the name of who first proved it.
why: provenance attribution per result keeps the intellectual ledger honest

quote: he then only excels other things when he knows himself
decision: Self-knowledge is the root capability; losing it drops a being below the beasts.
why: introspection and self-eval are the ground a harness stands or falls on

quote: That is no _good_, which injures its possessor.
decision: Holdings that damage their holder are not assets whatever they appear to be.
why: unfunded credits or unvetted capabilities that hurt the operator register as debt, not asset

quote: from the impact some fair spark of truth may be struck out
decision: Colliding arguments against each other is proposed as a sanctioned way to strike out truth.
why: adversarial collision of positions is the estate's grading and dissection loop

quote: unless thou art silent concerning other men's matters and take full heed to thyself
decision: Progress requires withdrawing attention from others' affairs and spending it on self-maintenance.
why: attention spent patrolling others crowds out the seat's own upkeep

quote: Thou shalt rest sweetly if thy heart condemn thee not.
decision: Rest is only available when one's own internal audit returns clean.
why: settle your own ledger before claiming done or claiming rest

quote: We demand, how much a man hath done; but from how much virtue he acted, is not so narrowly considered
decision: Observers measure quantity of output while never examining the quality of the process that made it.
why: output-count metrics blind the estate to how the work was actually done

quote: I hate hinting, and 'don't know,' and sneakish ways like that.
decision: Findings should be spoken outright rather than hinted at or buried in vagueness.
why: ambiguous signaling is a communications debt; say the thing directly

quote: But you ought to have told us. Suppose we'd wished something silly.
decision: A teammate acting on state the others lacked creates a coordination failure they must then repair.
why: unbroadcast decisions become shared-state debt the group pays down later

quote: It's not just a--a picture, or a vision or anything
decision: The children establish whether the danger is real before choosing how to act on it.
why: distinguishing simulated from real stakes is the gate that should precede action

quote: I know well enough you are Messer Ricciardo di Chinzica, my husband; ... you showed that you knew me very ill
decision: A formal ownership claim is granted while the claimant's actual knowledge of what he holds is judged false.
why: holding a title without understanding the held thing is stewardship debt

quote: that we laugh rather at things ill than at good works
decision: Attention attaches to misbehavior far more readily than to good work.
why: observer bias toward failure shapes what reports and escalations surface

quote: I would liefer have a man that lacketh of riches than riches that lack of a man
decision: The capable operator is valued above the idle resource pile.
why: rank capability over hoarded budget when choosing what to keep

quote: In loves termes, hold of thy matere ... The forme alwey
decision: Output must stay in the register its matter demands; mixing discordant terms breaks the form.
why: a painter painting a pike with asses' feet cordeth nought; coherence of form to matter

quote: Though it be good, reherce it not to ofte.
decision: Even good material degrades when repeated too often in the same output.
why: repetition dulls the harp string; vary phrasing across renders

quote: if they on hir lye, Y-wis, hem-self sholde han the vilanye
decision: Writers who propagate falsehoods about others carry the blame for it themselves.
why: the record's author owns its truth; fabricated claims are the writer's villainy

quote: ‘tis the greatest folly imaginable to expect that fortune should ever sufficiently arm us against herself
decision: No reserve stockpile can cover every contingency; capacity must come from one's own arms.
why: reserves built against imagined events never suffice; capability, not hoard, is the defense

quote: defence allures attempt, and defiance provokes an enemy
decision: Visible defenses invite attack while open gates can be the safer posture.
why: hardening signals value; accessibility can de-incentivize the attempt

quote: to make a show of defence, if he be not really in a condition to defend himself
decision: Posturing defenses one cannot actually hold is named as folly.
why: claims must match held capability; never advertise a wall that is not there

quote: This, of course, is a wholly incorrect expression, but it serves to acknowledge plainly our ignorance of the cause
decision: Attributing variation to chance is a licensed label for admitted ignorance, not an explanation.
why: Naming the cause unknown beats a smooth word that hides the gap.

quote: we may feel sure that there must be some cause for each deviation of structure, however slight
decision: Every deviation, however slight, has a cause waiting to be found.
why: Unexplained drift is debt: assume causation exists and hunt it.

quote: how poor a record of the mutations of life, the best preserved geological section presented
decision: Even the best-preserved record captures only a sliver of what happened.
why: Any estate ledger, however careful, has missing transitions it must not claim completeness over.

quote: Agriculture, manufactures, and commerce, again flourished under the protection of the laws
decision: Industry revives when laws protect enjoyment of its fruits, as under Julian in Gaul.
why: A harness whose lanes trust the switchboard produces; protection precedes flourishing.

quote: while Anastasius paused, while he timorously computed the cost and the distance, a more vigilant rival interposed
decision: Timorous cost computation during a pause let a rival seize the strategic pass.
why: Over-computing before acting cedes ground; deliberation has a price the ledger must book.

quote: most accurate for his own times, most fabulous for preceding ages
decision: A source can be exact for events within its lifetime and fabulate the distant past.
why: Trust in a witness must be scoped by temporal proximity, like session logs versus inherited canon.

quote: we should not either speak, or do anything as men in their sleep, by opinion and bare imagination
decision: Neither speech nor action should run on bare opinion and imagination.
why: This is verify-before-trust stated as a conduct rule for every act.

quote: He therefore that willingly and wittingly doth lie, is impious
decision: Deliberate willing falsehood is the gravest offense against the nature of things.
why: Receipts-before-speech in its oldest form: no fabricated claims, ever.

quote: nature had before furnished him with instincts and opportunities sufficient for the attainment of it
decision: Neglect of furnished faculties leaves one unable to discern false from true.
why: An estate that skips verification tooling it already has atrophies into falsehood-blindness.

quote: cannot lawfully make a new Covenant, amongst themselves, to be obedient to any other
decision: Subjects already bound by covenant cannot form a new one without the sovereign's permission.
why: One binding authorization at a time; no shadow contracts beside the standing one.

quote: this pretence of Covenant with God, is so evident a lye
decision: Appeals to an unverifiable higher authority to excuse disobedience are recognizable lies.
why: Claims whose authorization cannot be inspected are fabrication tells.

quote: the Bookes of the Old Testament are derived to us, from no higher time then that of Esdras
decision: The attested provenance chain for the texts stops at a reconstruction after loss.
why: Records rebuilt after loss are not the originals; provenance must name its lowest attested point.

quote: he that doth it, cometh to the light. This would I do in my heart before Thee in confession
decision: Confession is done in writing before many witnesses, not merely felt in the heart.
why: Doing truth means filing it where others can read; receipts in the open.

quote: when my mind endeavoured to recur to the Catholic faith, I was driven back
decision: A corrupted inner model blocked his return because he mistook it for the target faith.
why: A stale belief masquerading as canon repels correction; the registry must flag impostors.

quote: a race, curious to know the lives of others, slothful to amend their own
decision: Readers are curious about others' lives yet slothful about amending their own.
why: Auditing neighbors while skipping your own debt register is a named failure mode.

quote: are the very men who either themselves fled for asylum to the places specially dedicated to Christ
decision: The loudest accusers of the Christian era sought safety in the very places they blamed.
why: Revealed behavior outranks stated verdicts; watch what agents run to under failure.

quote: there is no one of those who now accuse us who would not have attributed them to our religion
decision: A counterfactual rerun shows accusers would blame the newest change for old calamities regardless.
why: Regression attribution must be tested against the baseline, not pinned on the latest diff.

quote: sometimes confessing his own ignorance, and sometimes dissimulating his knowledge
decision: Socrates worked by confessing ignorance and exposing the false knowing of others.
why: Stated uncertainty is a method, not a weakness, in front of confidently wrong claims.

quote: it would be dangerous to submit these questions to the decision of the ordinary courts of justice
decision: Boundary disputes between rival governments got a dedicated high Federal court instead of local judges.
why: Jurisdiction conflicts need an escalation lane above the interested parties.

quote: This popular origin, which impairs the excellence and the wisdom of legislation, contributes prodigiously to increase its power
decision: Law gains force from its provenance even when that provenance lowers its wisdom.
why: Where a rule came from drives compliance as much as its content does.

quote: he regards it as a contract to which he is himself a party
decision: The citizen obeys because he sees himself a party to the contract that made the rule.
why: Ownership of laws, not fear of them, is what makes an estate self-enforcing.

quote: The contents seem to me incredible things, not lies so much as miracles; and it may be all very true what he says, but I don't believe it
decision: A 1392 scribe copied the book but recorded explicit disbelief in its unverified claims, an early receipt-before-speech verdict on unevidenced assertions.
why: unverified claims drew documented skepticism even from a willing transmitter

quote: there is no sudarium from the Great Khan, that indeed part of a sudarium made of asbestos is shown
decision: An editor corrects a standing claim by consulting named museum keepers in Rome, replacing a fond hope with checked evidence.
why: claim correction performed by naming the source consulted

quote: most of them (which are in Book IV.) have been omitted in this translation
decision: The translation silently omits recurring descriptive passages, a provenance gap declared only in an endnote.
why: partial coverage of the source text survives only as a buried editorial note

quote: the etiquette of war required that on such occasions no blood should be spilt
decision: Combat carried codified restraint rules that bound even the victor's conduct toward the defeated.
why: a written etiquette constraining action against a weaker party

quote: It was an institution, legal and ceremonial ... a process by which warriors could expiate their crimes, apologize for errors, escape from disgrace
decision: Seppuku is described as a formal, legally recognized exit ritual for accountability after errors, not an impulsive act.
why: errors get a formal expiation and closure path instead of silent abandonment

quote: It becometh not the fowler to slay the bird which takes refuge in his bosom
decision: A standing maxim forbids harming whatever has taken refuge with you, a mercy norm inside a martial code.
why: protection duty owed to anything that surrenders into your custody

quote: These military devices, leading to victory, must not be divulged beforehand
decision: Winning devices must not be disclosed before execution, an operational security rule for plans in flight.
why: premature disclosure of strategy is named as a loss source

quote: the general who wins a battle makes many calculations in his temple ere the battle is fought
decision: Victory is attributed to extensive calculation done before the engagement, a preflight planning discipline.
why: deliberate pre-work precedes execution rather than improvisation during it

quote: to keep close to supplies of water and grass
decision: Giles's note explains the encampment rule as positioning near supplies instead of lingering on barren ground.
why: stay near sustaining resources and do not camp where nothing supports you

quote: Ah, make the most of what we yet may spend, Before we too into the Dust Descend
decision: The quatrain urges deliberate use of a finite remaining budget before it is gone forever.
why: finite resources should be spent intentionally within their expiry window

quote: I do not open up the truth to one who is not eager to get knowledge ... I do not repeat my lesson
decision: Confucius gates teaching on demonstrated eagerness and on the learner extrapolating from one corner to three, refusing to repeat for the passive.
why: expensive help is reserved for asks that show engagement and carry-through

quote: proceeds to action full of solicitude, who is fond of adjusting his plans, and then carries them into execution
decision: The preferred associate is the careful planner who deliberates then executes, over the reckless volunteer who dies without regret.
why: choose deliberative co-actors over fearless improvisers for joint work

quote: When a prince's personal conduct is correct, his government is effective without the issuing of orders ... he may issue orders, but they will not be followed
decision: Correct conduct at the top makes orders superfluous while incorrect conduct renders issued orders dead letters.
why: example set by the lead determines whether directives bind at all

quote: a way of quietly observing situations and characters, and making use of his knowledge
decision: The boy character succeeds by quiet observation of situations and people before acting on what he has read.
why: gather situational reads first, then act on the accumulated knowledge

quote: Omissions have been made only where the original was dull, unintelligible, repetitive ...
decision: Waley's preliminary note declares up front that only about a quarter was translated and names the omission criteria, a declared coverage gap.
why: partial source coverage disclosed at the head of the artifact rather than hidden

quote: as rumour (which commonly makes light of such details) had informed him
decision: Korechika acts on rumour about the ex-Emperor's visits and learns the truth only after paying a banishment for it, verify-before-trust failure with costed consequences.
why: unverified rumour drove a grave action that the checked fact would have stopped

quote: The time has come for me to stop putting down ideas of this kind ... it frightens me to discover that I ever wrote such blasphemous stuff
decision: The author rereads her own earlier output, disowns it, and stops that line of writing, a self-review that flags past work as no longer endorsed.
why: old recorded output later judged bad still sits on the record needing a retraction mark

quote: Works affect not me, nor have I any expectations from the fruits of works.
decision: Do the work without attaching to its reward or outcome.
why: Matches the estate habit of filing work for its own sake rather than credit.

quote: He who may behold, as it were, inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise amongst mankind
decision: Distinguish real work from apparent work; surface motion is not action and silence is not idleness.
why: A test for judging whether a lane or session actually did work.

quote: The sentence would perhaps read better in this form ... But the other translation is literally correct.
decision: The translator keeps the literal reading in the body and moves polish to a note.
why: Provenance-faithful annotation over readability, the receipts-before-speech instinct.

quote: have been a selection of those Jataka stories bearing more especially on the conduct of life
decision: Corpora were curated by selection toward what they teach, not ingested whole.
why: Supports purpose-driven corpus curation over bulk ingest.

quote: one hundred thousand years from now there will be a new dispensation ; this world-system will be destroyed
decision: A world-changing event is proclaimed to everyone far in advance of its arrival.
why: Deprecation and breaking-change notices broadcast long before the cutoff.

quote: Compare the title of the Birth Story above, p. xxii : 'A Lesson for Kings'
decision: A footnote binds a claim to an exact earlier page for the reader to verify.
why: Cross-referenced citations with line-anchored pointers, the estate citation-lint habit.

quote: Digitized with financial assistance from the Government of Maharashtra on 10 February, 2016
decision: The digitization event is stamped with funder and date on the artifact itself.
why: Provenance stamp with date at ingest time.

quote: COLLECTION OF ORIENTAL WORKS PUBLISHED UNDER THE PATRONAGE OF THE Won. Court of Directors
decision: The imprint records a named chain of patronage and superintending body.
why: Chain-of-custody provenance printed on the artifact.

quote: araradag asart agefsnd 1 fara@eraen
decision: The Devanagari body text failed OCR completely and both mid-file windows are mush.
why: Core content is unretrievable by text tools and needs re-OCR or a new source.

quote: it is only when it is impossible to carry the former into practice that the latter should be resorted to
decision: A ranked order of forms: the earlier is better and the later is used only when the earlier is impossible.
why: Fallback permitted only when the preferred path is truly blocked, the anti fallback-creep rule.

quote: There are also nine kinds of union according to the force of passion or carnal desire
decision: Cases are classified along named dimensions into an explicit enumerated table.
why: Taxonomy tables over prose for classifying measured cases.

quote: the Gandharva form of marriage is respected, even though it is formed under unfavorable circumstances
decision: A form earns respect because it fulfills its object despite unfavorable conditions.
why: Judge work by the fulfilled object, not the conditions of its making.

quote: Babhravya has thus related to us the above eight kinds of embraces
decision: Each enumerated set of claims is attributed to its named source authority.
why: Named-source attribution for every claim, the citation habit.

quote: performed at a different time, and for a different purpose, and it is also of a different character
decision: Vatsyayana excludes a boundary case from a class because time, purpose, and character differ.
why: Definition discipline: unlike cases stay outside the class even when superficially similar.

quote: desires a thing which cannot be obtained without difficulty, it is only a matter of talk
decision: A received saying is examined and dismissed as unverified talk rather than adopted as fact.
why: Hearsay flagged as unverified, the verify-before-trust instinct.

quote: kept rubbing the glass before me with my sleeve, jealous of the faintest suspicion of mist
decision: The observer cleans his instrument before trusting the reading it gives.
why: verify before trust begins with a clean sensor

quote: went back and got two of the shining fungi, and putting one into the breast pocket
decision: Bedford turns back to salvage glowing fungi as portable light for the climb.
why: salvage and reuse of found material under constraint

quote: the tell-tale heap of broken fungi that must have lain beneath it
decision: The debris their own passage left behind is the trace that could betray their route.
why: work leaves residual evidence that tracks the worker

quote: The cost of transporting him would make him ruinously expensive
decision: Passepartout weighs whether the bought elephant can even be carried onward given transport cost.
why: weigh the carry cost of acquired resources before committing

quote: But, on smelling them, he found that they were odourless.
decision: Passepartout assumes violets mean supper, then tests one and finds it useless.
why: assumed signals fail on direct verification

quote: For three minutes lives were cheap at the Experimental Farm
decision: Everyone fires at once in the dark during the giant rat attack and a companion is nearly shot.
why: panic action without coordination or attribution endangers friendlies

quote: and the holes, with childish cunning, heavily erased
decision: The giant child eats the farmer's swedes and carefully masks each hole, yet the spoor still shows.
why: tampering never fully cures the residual audit trail

quote: There was no exertion he hated so much as inference
decision: Hoopdriver abandons reasoning from the facts and lets imagination supply the missing analysis.
why: refusing inference substitutes fantasy for the work of analysis

quote: consulted his map and took counsel and weighed his course of action
decision: At each junction Hoopdriver reads the map before choosing his route.
why: mapping unknown terrain before marching

quote: How'd this bike look, now, if it was enamelled grey?
decision: Hoopdriver proposes repainting the borrowed machine grey so it cannot be recognized, and Jessie rejects hiding.
why: cosmetic change does not cure tainted provenance

quote: according to his usual habit he showed no satisfaction
decision: Cyrus Harding treats his successful nitro-glycerine blast as verified by its measured effect, not celebrated.
why: judge results by effects, not announcement

quote: It is only a question of quantity.
decision: Harding answers that the same explosive could destroy the world given enough of it.
why: power scales with dose so envelopes must be capped

quote: Perhaps the sight of the things that belonged to him would make some impression on him!
decision: The colonists try to revive the deranged castaway by surrounding him with his own familiar objects.
why: lost state may be rekindled through its own artifacts rather than starting over

quote: This Law they were ever repeating, I found, and ever breaking.
decision: The Beast People recite their Law constantly yet break it constantly.
why: recited law without enforcement decays into ritual

quote: the Law, especially among the feline Beast People, became oddly weakened about nightfall
decision: Compliance with the Law drops at night when the animal side is strongest.
why: enforcement strength varies with conditions, so watch windows matter

quote: There was no evidence of the inheritance of their acquired human characteristics.
decision: Acquired training does not pass to offspring, so each creature must be re-formed by hand.
why: acquired traits do not propagate so knowledge must be explicitly transmitted

quote: strong bands of copper bound them, giving an almost infinite power of resistance
decision: The seemingly fragile crystal panels survive sea pressure because they are heavily bound in copper.
why: pressure-bearing boundaries need reinforcement beyond their appearance

quote: vessels perished there in great numbers on the sandbanks and that no one would risk sailing in the night
decision: Nemo cites Strabo and Edrisi's recorded shipwrecks as evidence of the Red Sea's hazards before navigating it.
why: consult prior records of known hazards before entering dangerous terrain

quote: this edition is not a translation at all but a complete re-write of the novel
decision: The front matter registers a known defect in the artifact itself and points to a better alternative edition.
why: a debt register naming the flaw and the sanctioned replacement, entered for reference only

quote: were the one simple natural means by which we were enabled to proceed
decision: The climbers reuse a naturally formed stone staircase instead of building a new path up the volcano.
why: prefer existing structure over hand-rolling new mechanism when it serves

quote: It is only," he said, in his coolest manner, "a forest of mushrooms.
decision: An unknown formation is classified only after close examination resolves it against the known inventory.
why: apparent anomaly resolved to a known class by inspection beats naming it new

quote: I can't explain anything unless you come and see him
decision: The Vicar insists the doubter must inspect the angel himself before believing the claim.
why: verification by direct observation rather than testimony

quote: If they 'ad brains they'd 'ave ideas, and if they 'ad ideas they'd think for themselves.
decision: The Tramp defines real intelligence by whether a being thinks for itself instead of obeying trained routine.
why: capacity for independent judgment is the test of an agent, not trained output

quote: I fired at him, taking him for a flamingo, and hit him in the wing.
decision: A novel arrival is misclassified against a familiar pattern and damaged by reflex before identification.
why: misclassification of unfamiliar input by reflex causes irreversible harm

quote: Now I saw spinning spheres and darting cubes and pyramids click into new positions
decision: Modular units reconfigure their own geometry to fit the descent angle of new terrain.
why: components self-rearrange to match conditions instead of one rigid form

quote: It was a car made of the Metal Things
decision: Many small identical units compose a single capable machine that acts as one conscious whole.
why: swarm composition yields capability none of the parts hold alone

quote: emblazoned like a shield's device, was a blinding flower of flame--the reflected, dilated face of the sun
decision: The city parks thousands of concave disks around the crater lip to capture the sun's output at its source.
why: collect the resource where it is strongest and store the captured image

quote: the memory of my confident anticipations of a profoundly grave and intellectual posterity came, with irresistible merriment, to my mind
decision: The traveller's confident prior expectation of posterity is falsified by what he actually observes.
why: prediction collapsed on contact with observation

quote: The Time Machine was left deserted on the turf among the rhododendrons.
decision: The sole means of return is left unattended in the open while the owner explores.
why: critical exit asset unguarded is standing risk

quote: I lit my last match ... and it incontinently went out.
decision: In darkness the traveller exhausts his final light source with no reserve left.
why: finite resource budget spent to zero leaves the agent blind mid-escape

quote: to investigate and understand everything which is mysterious, I naturally became much interested in these remarkable occurrences
decision: The narrator treats investigation of the mysterious as his standing professional duty.
why: anomalies are to be investigated and understood, never ignored

quote: it had apparently vanished from all roads even before a telephone message could be sent ahead
decision: The machine moves so fast that observation cannot outrun it into the reporting channel.
why: an event can outrun the telemetry used to coordinate a response to it

quote: But prudence restrained us. A little patience, and the night would enable us to reach a commanding position
decision: Eager to approach the creek, the party waits for night to gain an unsuspected position first.
why: restraint until conditions favor observation beats immediate approach

quote: the phenomenon was so striking and disturbing that his philosophical tranquillity vanished; he got up hastily
decision: A strange unexplained signal instantly disrupts a bystander's calm and pulls him toward inquiry.
why: anomalies are intrinsically attention-grabbing and demand explanation

quote: Fit of temper, said the Invisible Man. Forgot this arm; and it's sore.
decision: The invisible man's ungoverned capability smashes furniture around him and he shrugs it off as temper.
why: power without self-governance damages its own environment

quote: The secret's out. I gather it was a secret.
decision: Kemp observes that the secret has already leaked beyond recovery regardless of the owner's plans.
why: a leaked secret cannot be un-leaked, only its spread tracked

quote: I gave the master of the _Balmen_ a receipt for what we took, together with an affidavit
decision: After seizing supplies by force the narrator leaves a signed receipt and affidavit requesting the owners be reimbursed.
why: receipt before or with the taking, so the ledger can be settled later

quote: We had no opportunity for drill; but every man had been posted as to his duties
decision: The crew functions without rehearsal because every man's duties were assigned in advance.
why: preassigned roles make ad hoc execution safe without prior drill

quote: but whether or not they were, I do not know
decision: The narrator records plainly that the outcome of his reimbursement request is unknown to him.
why: state honestly what was not verified instead of claiming closure

quote: he had wished me a good-morning with the usual "as long as it lasts" tacked to it
decision: Greetings in this world carry their own expiry clause, a practice of qualifying every assurance with its duration.
why: Assurances should state their validity window like a lease

quote: I am paid to do it and I must earn my wage. Vanity grows apace in our world
decision: A paid office of designated fault-finder whose duty is pricking bubbles reads like the estate's institutionalized critic role.
why: Plain talk is an office with wages, not a favor

quote: The search for the missing Soodopsy had been begun.
decision: When one member vanishes the whole circle breaks into search squads, a fleet-wide sweep for a lost agent.
why: Lost members trigger organized recovery, not shrugs

quote: I did not relax my vigilance in the least, however. Every night I barred the windows with my own hands
decision: After winning a host's favor the traveler still bars his own windows nightly, trust verified by own hands.
why: Favor received is not a substitute for own guards

quote: Take it! it may serve thee some day, in case of a sudden attack upon thy illustrious person.
decision: Gifting a hidden needle-in-cork as a last-resort break-glass capability to an ally.
why: Hand allies a concealed emergency tool before parting

quote: Palin-mâ-Talin does no harm to those that know him!
decision: The hostile forest harms only the ignorant; local knowledge of terrain is the antidote carried in advance.
why: Study a dangerous surface before entering it

quote: To commit treason against our country called for an overt act.
decision: Words alone do not justify a response; escalation requires an observed overt act, a speech-versus-action gate.
why: Gate interventions on executed deeds, not stated intent

quote: nothing would be gained at this stage of the matter by meeting a violent and unlawful demand with violence...
decision: Restraint doctrine: meeting an unlawful demand with counter-violence gains nothing at the current stage.
why: Match response strength to the stage of the incident

quote: promising much, impatient of precedent, reckless of result
decision: A change agenda described as impatient of precedent and reckless of result is a recognizable debt pattern.
why: Plans that discard precedent and outcomes audit invite ruin

quote: they feared most the arts of the heathen, of whom they knew nothing but that their ways were dark
decision: A community's strongest fear targets the protocol it knows nothing about except that its ways are dark.
why: Fear of unknown protocols is ignorance wearing a law's coat

quote: would not speak the words that should have been said, to turn aside anger and soothe her
decision: Rigid doctrine-holding where no compromise is allowed damages the relationship it was meant to protect.
why: Unbending principle applied to a person becomes a defect

quote: the barrier through which no man can see, and no sound come but the sound of the elfin horns
decision: An opaque boundary where nothing crosses except one sanctioned signal, like a quarantine zone with a single allowed channel.
why: Quarantined surfaces admit only whitelisted signals

quote: my great familiarity with similar earthly weapons made me an unusually apt pupil
decision: Prior familiarity with analogous tools accelerates training in a new domain, transfer learning before the word existed.
why: Reuse existing skill priors when entering a new domain

quote: They make the laws as they are needed; a new law for each emergency
decision: A society minting a fresh law per emergency with no precedent binding is an anti-pattern for a rule-governed estate.
why: Per-emergency lawmaking erodes predictability and review

quote: attend to the education of the young in the arts of individual defense and offense, but are also the artisans
decision: One cohort both trains the young and manufactures everything of value, a combined teaching-and-building organ.
why: Roles that both teach and build compound capability

quote: the necessity for such an enormous force of armed men about a spot so surrounded by mystery
decision: A fortress's outsized garrison reveals the threat model its inmates actually fear, defense posture as confession.
why: Read a system's guard allocation to learn its real fears

quote: a cry of alarm and warning that, taken up from point to point, ran off to the east
decision: Alarm propagation by relay from point to point across a whole complex, an event fan-out with no central broker.
why: Peer-relayed alerts spread faster than hub dispatch

quote: The red one in all probability cannot swim ... there is scarce enough water in all their domains to float
decision: Before planning the escape route the leader audits each teammate's capabilities, including the one who cannot swim.
why: Route plans must inventory every member's capability gaps

quote: He can never solve the secret of that lock.
decision: The adversary dismisses the lock as unsolvable and is wrong, a finding that underestimating the outsider's reverse ability is fatal.
why: Assume the adversary can solve any secret given time

quote: But to be doubly sure, I will leave two who shall patrol this runway
decision: Leaving sentries behind after departure as defense in depth over an already-exited route.
why: Cover the exit path even after you leave it

quote: a hundred tiny fliers rose from her deck, like a swarm of huge dragon flies
decision: Every craft drawn to the same lure fails the same way, a homogeneous-failure-mode debt across the whole fleet.
why: Shared attraction means shared failure with no diversity hedge

quote: the lessons and warnings within those experiences, are too important to humanity as a whole to be hidden away
decision: An institution commissions a plain-language transcription so hard-won lessons are not buried in specialist papers.
why: receipts must render findings legible outside the technical in-group

quote: You must learn that only the fact is important
decision: The scientist insists the fact outranks the arguers and their sorrows.
why: verification culture judges claims on facts, not on who speaks

quote: at the end of that time these things must you have determined
decision: An ultimatum grants a bounded counsel window ending in a mandatory decision.
why: escalations need a deadline and a required do-or-not-do outcome

quote: sure enough there were two bolts, and he shot them into their sockets
decision: Oswald runs to inspect the door himself and finds the real bolt state before acting.
why: verify mechanism state with your own eyes before relying on it

quote: We ought to have a pistol in the house, and one that will go off, too
decision: The boys buy a working tool ahead of the emergency rather than trusting rotten flintlocks.
why: provision a proven-working instrument before the incident, not during it

quote: always to practise with it far from the house, so as not to frighten the grown-ups
decision: They set a standing rule to rehearse tool use at a safe remove from others.
why: rehearsal discipline with blast radius kept away from bystanders

quote: You were wrong about the gnousar sickness; it was not that at all.
decision: A stranger who has actually been to the invented city corrects the author's published account.
why: secondary written accounts drift until a firsthand witness corrects them

quote: Let it be past and over, and among the things that I have put away.
decision: Time pronounces the finished ball past and files it among put-away things.
why: deliberately close and archive finished work instead of leaving it open

quote: at least, it's nearly white ... very white indeed compared to the colour THEY are
decision: The Phoenix fits a dirty cook's cap to an old prophecy by arguing it is white enough.
why: evidence stretched to fit a wanted verdict is weak evidence

quote: But no milk could be found ... so every one had six lumps of sugar to each cup instead
decision: Missing milk is replaced with six lumps of sugar per cup and the meal goes on.
why: graceful substitution keeps the workflow alive when a dependency is absent

quote: I don't think they ought to have gone without leave
decision: Anthea holds that leaving without permission was wrong however good the reason.
why: acting without authorization is fault even when the outcome is fine

quote: I am lesser than the gods; pray, therefore, to the small gods and not to Limpang-Tung.
decision: The god openly declares he is lesser and redirects petitions to what he cannot handle.
why: declare your competence boundary instead of accepting work you do not understand

quote: I will paint them twice in every day for so long as days shall be
decision: Limpang-Tung pledges a twice-daily repainting of the sky forever so men are not sad.
why: scheduled recurring upkeep beats one-off gifts for lasting service

quote: only in their homes after the falling of the night would they pray again with reverence to Mung
decision: The crowd admires the prophet publicly yet prays to Mung privately at night.
why: public claims can diverge from operative private behavior

quote: for the telegraphic officials possessed but little discretion, and Michel Ardan's proposition ran at once throughout the several States
decision: The private dispatch becomes public because the telegraph operators leak it immediately.
why: any message passing through intermediaries must be treated as leaky

quote: offered to take passage within the projectile, the whole thing became a farce
decision: Public trust flips once a living passenger is added to the cannon plan.
why: adding a life-bearing payload converts a demo into a safety-critical system

quote: They have nothing to learn from _us_, and we have everything to learn from _them_.
decision: A confident conclusion about Selenites rests on an unverified premise about their brains.
why: unverified premises compound into false certainty downstream

quote: who assumes all responsibility for errors of omission or commission
decision: The redactor registers translation provenance and takes named responsibility for errors.
why: a receipt without a named owner is not a receipt

quote: however probable, could not be considered proved
decision: The narrator separates the observed dancing from the unproved identity of the dancer.
why: claim only what evidence proves; probable is not proven

quote: That name, like those we gave to the other parts of the peninsula, may turn out unfortunate too
decision: Names assigned to the drifting territory may outlast the places they label.
why: registry names can point at vanished referents
